coverage_gaps: Whether elevated LRRK2 kinase activity is a broadly reproducible feature of idiopathic Parkinson disease may remain underdetermined because biomarker assays, tissues, and cohorts differ.
The hierarchy of Rab substrates that are physiological in human dopaminergic neurons may remain uncertain despite strong biochemical and peripheral-tissue evidence.
Direct causal links from individual phospho-Rab events to nigrostriatal degeneration may be weaker than links to trafficking, lysosomal, or ciliary phenotypes.
Penetrance and effect estimates may remain ancestry-biased for rare pathogenic and population-specific risk variants.
Human interventional evidence available by the cutoff may establish target engagement and safety more readily than disease modification.
Public FDA materials may yield little mechanistic evidence for investigational LRRK2 inhibitors; a null regulatory search must be recorded without treating it as proof of biological inefficacy.
Apparent disagreement may persist because overexpression, knock-in, knockout, acute inhibitor, peripheral-cell, brain-tissue, and animal systems probe different biological contexts.
exclusion_criteria: Articles that mention LRRK2 or Parkinson disease only incidentally and contribute no genetic, biochemical, physiological, translational, or limiting evidence.
Variant assertions lacking an identifiable cohort, segregation observation, association analysis, functional result, or authoritative classification basis.
Purely in silico substrate or pathway predictions without experimental validation.
Non-Parkinson disease studies unless they directly test conserved LRRK2 enzymology, substrate biology, physiological function, or treatment liability relevant to the mechanism.
Duplicate reports of the same cohort or experiment when they add no independent data, while retaining the most complete record and linking companion reports.
Narrative claims traceable only to secondary citation chains when the corresponding primary evidence can be retrieved.
Clinical or regulatory records with no LRRK2-directed intervention, biomarker, genotype-defined population, or interpretable relevance to the proposed mechanism.
inclusion_criteria: Publication, registry submission, or regulatory record is dated on or before 2024-12-31.

Evidence directly addresses LRRK2 discovery, Parkinson disease association, variant effects, enzyme regulation, physiological substrates, downstream physiology, target engagement, or limitations on those claims.
Major historical and mechanistic claims are anchored to primary studies; reviews may supply terminology, context, and citation backtracking.
Human genetic studies report enough information to identify the variant, population, phenotype, and direction of association or penetrance estimate.
A substrate study provides evidence of LRRK2-dependent phosphorylation through biochemical, genetic, pharmacological, structural, or endogenous-system validation.
Experimental-model studies are eligible when model, perturbation, expression context, and relevance to Parkinson disease can be stated explicitly.
Negative, null, contradictory, replication, safety, and model-limitation evidence is eligible under the same relevance and date standards as supportive evidence.
Clinical trial and regulatory records are eligible when they clarify intervention status, enrolled genotype or disease population, target engagement, outcomes, safety, or approval status.

queries.query: LRRK2 AND Parkinson AND (systematic review OR meta-analysis OR consensus OR review[Publication Type]) AND ("2023/01/01"[Date - Publication] : "2024/12/31"[Date - Publication])

question_frame: As of 2024-12-31, assess how human LRRK2 genetics established a relationship with Parkinson disease; distinguish causal, risk-modifying, protective, and uncertain variants; connect ROC-COR GTPase and kinase biochemistry to endogenous physiological substrates and cellular phenotypes; and test how well those mechanisms generalize across variant carriers, idiopathic Parkinson disease, experimental systems, ancestries, and therapeutic perturbations. Scope includes historical genetic discovery, penetrance and population heterogeneity, enzymatic regulation, substrate validation, disease-relevant physiology, human biomarkers, interventional evidence, and explicit contradictory or limiting evidence.
stop_rules: Complete at least one sentinel, discovery, confirmation, challenge, and update wave and execute every route listed in source_map.
Do not stop until the genetic chronology includes linkage, gene identification, major high-penetrance variants, population risk variants, protective signals, penetrance, and ancestry limitations.
Do not stop until kinase and ROC-COR GTPase mechanisms are separately evaluated and their proposed coupling is supported or qualified with primary evidence.

For each substrate presented as physiological, require direct phosphorylation evidence plus at least one orthogonal endogenous, genetic, pharmacological, structural, or rescue validation; downgrade candidates that do not meet this rule.

Require at least one deliberately retrieved limiting or contradictory source for each major bridge from variant to enzyme activity, enzyme activity to substrate, substrate to cellular phenotype, and cellular phenotype to Parkinson disease.

Require explicit comparison among pathogenic-variant carriers, idiopathic Parkinson disease, healthy controls, and experimental models wherever evidence exists; record unavailable comparisons as coverage gaps.
Continue targeted backfill until two consecutive query refinements add no new qualified concept, variant class, substrate class, causal bridge, or material contradiction.
Reconcile trial status and regulatory status through records current to the cutoff, including completed, terminated, withdrawn, and negative studies when present.

Stop citation expansion when every major claim has a primary source, all retained disagreements are represented, duplicate cohorts are resolved, and remaining uncertainty is documented rather than filled by inference.
Exclude any evidence crossing the temporal cutoff even if it would alter the conclusion.
